title: Authorization policy domain service
description: Implement the central policy object that answers: can this user view this task, edit its title/description, assign it, transition it to a given status, comment on it, view this project, view this team, transfer team lead or project ownership. Encode the spec rules precisely, including: a Project Owner may create tasks and edit title/description but may only move Draft->Todo or cancel; a Project Owner cannot be assigned a task in their own project; a Team Lead assigns tasks only within their own teams' projects and only to members of that project's team, and may assign to themselves; a Team Lead sees all non-Draft tasks in their teams' projects; a Team Member sees tasks that are neither Draft nor Canceled in projects of their teams. This is the highest-risk piece of the system - it must be derived line by line from docs/authorization.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every rule in docs/authorization.md has a corresponding passing test, including the negative cases; policy returns the distinction between forbidden and not-found where leaking existence would be inappropriate.
close_reason: Domain layer implemented under backend/src/main/kotlin/hive/domain with 486 passing unit tests and 100% line coverage on hive.domain.

title: Task entity, TaskStatus and the transition state machine
description: Implement Task (id, name, description, project, creator, assignee nullable, status defaulting to Draft) and the TaskStatus enum with the exact transition table from spec.md: Draft->Todo and Draft->Canceled by Project Owner; Todo->In Progress and In Progress->Completed by the assigned Team Member; Todo->Canceled and In Progress->Canceled by Project Owner; Completed and Canceled are terminal. Every other transition is a conflict. Also enforce that a Task in a terminal state cannot have its name, description, status or assignee changed. The transition function must take the acting user's relationship to the task (project owner / assignee / other) and return either the new state or the precise failure reason, distinguishing an illegal transition (409) from a forbidden one (403).
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive table-driven unit test covering every from-state x to-state x actor-role combination; terminal-state edit ban tested for name, description, status and assignee.
close_reason: Domain layer implemented under backend/src/main/kotlin/hive/domain with 486 passing unit tests and 100% line coverage on hive.domain.

title: OpenAPI documentation

comments.author: Adam <la-xirsoi> Chevalier
comments.text: Blocked on upstream: springdoc-openapi has no Spring Boot 4 / Spring Framework 7 release. Latest on Maven Central is 2.8.6 (Boot 3.x, javax/spring-web 6 APIs); org.springdoc 3.x artifacts are 2020-era demo poms, not a Boot 4 line. Per the task instruction, no downgrade was made to force it. /v3/api-docs/** and /swagger-ui/** are already permitAll in SecurityConfig, so adding the starter later needs no security change. Revisit when springdoc ships a Boot 4 compatible release.

title: EPIC: Containerization, quality gates and documentation
description: Podman Containerfiles for every component, compose stack including MS SQL Server 2022 and an OAuth identity provider, TLS config, coverage enforcement, seed data, and final project documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Containerfiles and compose file present and lint-clean; coverage gates fail the build below 70%; docs describe how to run the whole stack.

title: Add OpenAPI generation once springdoc supports Spring Boot 4
description: springdoc-openapi has no release compatible with Spring Boot 4 / Spring Framework 7 as of 2026-09-14; Maven Central's newest (2.8.6) targets Boot 3.x and the org.springdoc 3.x coordinates are unpopulated placeholder poms. The alternative, hand-authoring an openapi.yaml, was rejected: a hand-maintained document drifts from the code silently, which is worse than having none, and docs/api-contract.md already serves as the authoritative human-readable description. Revisit when springdoc ships Boot 4 support. No security change is needed - /v3/api-docs/** and /swagger-ui/** are already permitAll in SecurityConfig.
acceptance_criteria: springdoc starter added on a Boot 4 compatible version; generated document served and checked against docs/api-contract.md.
